title: Prefix atlas + compact slab allocator for cross-request KV deduplication
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Our runtime's per-request KV cache stores overlapping prompt prefixes as distinct fragments across GPUs which inflates GPU memory usage and lowers prefix hit-rate under mixed workloads. Shorter prompts (<= 128 tokens) have a low shared-prefix hit-rate (baseline ~18%) and cause repeated KV uploads between batches, increasing per-token GPU memory by ~22% and p50 latency by ~9ms under bursty traffic.

Goal: Implement a lightweight, cross-request prefix atlas (canonicalizer) plus a compact slab allocator for GPU-side KV fragments to deduplicate identical or semantically equivalent prefix fragments and pack them densely on-device. Targets: increase prefix hit-rate to >=60% for common prompt families, reduce KV GPU footprint by >=35% on average, and keep added CPU overhead <6% of request processing time.

High-level approach:
- Canonicalization: compute a stable content-hash for canonical prompt segments after deterministic normalization (whitespace trimming, placeholder canonicalization, small token-level rewrites) to map near-duplicate prefixes to a single signature.
- Prefix atlas: in the control plane on each host maintain a compact catalog mapping signatures -> device fragment locations and metadata (length, model-compatibility hash).
- Compact slab allocator: on the GPU runtime implement slab packing of KV fragments with allocation granularity tuned for attention head/kv alignment; this reduces internal fragmentation and enables reference-counted sharing across requests and sessions.
- Eviction and versioning: prefer LRU-ish policy with size-aware eviction and quick tombstone metadata to avoid serving stale KV for model version rollouts.
- Telemetry and safety: add hit/miss counters and verification hooks to ensure canonicalization does not change model outputs for guarded prompt sets.

Why different from existing work: Prior tickets focused on fragment coalescing and signature eviction; this ticket prioritizes a combined on-host signature atlas with a GPU allocator designed for dense packing and cross-request reference counting to minimize on-device memory fragmentation and inter-request transfer cost.
acceptance_criteria: Prefix atlas canonicalization increases measured cross-request prefix hit-rate from baseline (~18%) to >=60% on evaluation corpus of common prompts
End-to-end KV GPU memory used for short-prompt workloads reduces by >=35% in our synthetic benchmark (same model/devices)
p50 latency overhead of canonicalization + atlas lookup is <6ms and CPU overhead <6% of request CPU time for 99th-percentile host load
No detectable semantic regressions on guarded eval set: logits distribution drift <0.1 L2 across prompts where atlas is applied
Feature guarded behind runtime config flags and unit/regression tests exist; rollout plan defined and tested in staging

comments: 2026-03-10 - Triage: initial investigation shows repeated uploads of identical KV fragments across concurrent requests on same host; spike in device memory during morning traffic. Logged by Aisha.

2026-03-11 - Design sync: agreed on deterministic canonicalization (whitespace normalize + placeholder canonicalization). Luca noted risk for templated prompts; we will whitelist templates where canonicalization is permitted.

2026-03-12 - Prototype update: host-side atlas prototype implemented (in-memory Robin Hood map) and integrated into batching hot path. Microbench: atlas lookup cost ~1.8ms median on staging host under 75% load. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1034

2026-03-13 - GPU allocator prototype: early slab allocator implemented in GPU runtime; packing reduced internal fragmentation in synthetic test by 28%. Open PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/gpu-runtime/pull/211

2026-03-14 - Design review notes: PM flagged customer cases where privacy-sensitive templates must skip atlas. Added label-level opt-out and customer_impact review. Security to run deeper PII scan before enabling by default. Action: secure-review (security@redwood) assigned.

2026-03-14 - Next steps: finish refcount compaction correctness tests; add graceful fallback when atlas lookup fails; add integration tests exercising model rollouts and tombstones. Assigned to Luca and GPU infra leads.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy atlas+allocator behind feature flag to staging (1 week)
2) Run closed beta on low-risk customers with opt-in config (2 weeks)
3) Monitor telemetry for regressions (7 days), enable auto-rollback on anomalies
4) Gradually increase rollout to all hosts if metrics meet SLOs
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-aggressive canonicalization could alter outputs for templated prompts. Mitigation: whitelist templates and run guarded evals; keep feature gated.
Risk: GPU memory fragmentation during compaction may spike latency. Mitigation: run compaction incrementally during low load and throttle compaction work.
Risk: Atlas metadata could become a hotspot under very large catalogs. Mitigation: shard atlas per-host; set entry TTL and size caps; evict cold signatures.
Risk: PII leakage via shared fragments. Mitigation: allow customer opt-out, integrate KMS tagging for sensitive sessions, security review required before enablement.
